_readme: Trading settings shared by the Python engine and the NestJS API.
This file is the ONLY place the defaults live. Both runtimes read it at start.
An environment variable with the same name overrides a value (for experiments).
Percent fields ending in _PCT under 'costs' are percentages (0.03 = 0.03%).

RISK_PER_TRADE_PCT is a FRACTION (0.02 = 2%), never 2. It is taken of what a trade may deploy: the cell fund times its leverage. So an intraday trade (5x) may risk 2% of 50,000 = 1,000 rupees and a swing trade (1x) 2% of 10,000 = 200.
MAX_COST_TO_RISK: a trade is skipped when its round-trip cost (charges + slippage both ways) is more than this share of the rupees it risks. 0 turns the rule off.

LIFECYCLE_PAUSE_FUND_FLOOR_PCT: a cell is paused when its fund (starting fund plus the result of all its closed trades) has fallen to this share of the starting fund. 0.5 = paused when 5,000 of the 10,000 is left.

selection: the one rule that decides whether a cell's BACKTEST is good enough to go live (paper). Used by auto-select, by the roster and by the warning on the Set Live button. All of: average per trade above SELECT_MIN_AVG_R; positive in both halves of its history; at least SELECT_MIN_TRADES_INTRADAY, _SWING or _LONG trades (LONG is for the long-hold strategies, which signal only a few times per stock in five years); profit factor at least SELECT_MIN_PROFIT_FACTOR; net profit at least SELECT_MIN_PROFIT_TO_DRAWDOWN times the worst drawdown; total return at least SELECT_MIN_ROI_PCT percent of the fund; and, for swing, the strategy passes the first luck test.
lifecycle: when a cell (one stock with one strategy) is paused, resumed or marked proven. Judged on its closed paper trades after costs, in R (profit or loss divided by the rupees risked).

Slippage per share, each side, is the larger of TICK_SIZE (the smallest price step, in rupees) and BT_SLIPPAGE_BPS basis points of the price. For a cheap stock one tick is more than 5 basis points; for an expensive one it is less.
